items.title: Bob Watts Interview, 1963-02-28
items.q: And Lang would sit on my right side. I'd sit on top the old upright, take the front out, and I'd sit on top, just beat the side of it.

ctx.x: He's probably doing that, but I can't remember his name. He's one of them old-timers, too. I didn't catch him. He'd catch him around busters, you know. Oh, yeah?

Well, he was playing drums. This man's going to give us two dollars a night in this joint, three pieces. Had old beat-up piano back in the corner, one of them old uprights, you know. And Lang would sit on my right side. I'd sit on top the old upright, take the front out, and I'd sit on top, just beat the side of it. Me and my cornet, I had a con cornet. And I'm trying to think of the piano player. This boy was burnt pretty bad when he was a child. And his daddy used to pedal fruit on a wagon. They used to live on…
